To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the substitution of taxfiler data for census income data is an appropriate approach for developing neighbourhood SES indices, and the use of multiple principal components in the PCA process produces SES scores that are more distinct and therefore useful.

1) taxfiler income variables may be substituted for census income data in PCA to develop SES indices; 2) using multiple principal components produces clearer SES distinctions than using only a single principal component; and 3) the use of PCA is an appropriate and useful method for developing neighbourhood SES indices.

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) can be used as a useful tool in the development of socioeconomic status (SES) indices to identify area level disparities in SES within a community; and the substitution of taxfiler (income tax data) income variables for census (census data) income variables yielded SES index scores distributions and neighbourhood SES level classifications that were similar, and more distinct, to SES scores calculated from entirely census data variables.
